title: Production-Grade Distributed Raft Consensus Engine with Pre-Vote & Dynamic Reconfiguration
objective: Implement a complete, production-grade distributed Raft consensus cluster engine in C++20. The implementation must support Leader Election with randomized election timers, Log Replication, persistent state management, Log Compaction & Snapshotting (InstallSnapshot RPC), Pre-Vote protocol extension to prevent disruptive re-elections during network partitions, Linearizable Reads (ReadIndex optimization), and Joint Consensus dynamic cluster membership reconfiguration (C_old -> C_old_new -> C_new).
motivation: Distributed consensus engines (such as etcd, TiKV, CockroachDB) form the backbone of reliable cloud infrastructure. Minor state-machine oversights during uncommitted log overwrites, split-brain scenarios after asymmetric network partitions, or concurrent membership reconfigurations routinely induce catastrophic data loss.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Asymmetric Network Partitions & Pre-Vote: Preventing partitioned nodes from incrementing election terms and stepping down the active leader upon reconnecting by executing non-disruptive pre-vote rounds.
2. Joint Consensus Dynamic Membership Changes: Safely migrating cluster membership across overlapping quorum sets without split-brain or downtime.
3. Log Compaction & Streaming Snapshot Transfer: Managing log truncation and atomic snapshot installation for lagging/recovering replicas while simultaneously processing concurrent client write requests.
environmentSummary: Debian 12 container with gcc-13, g++-13, cmake 3.28, ninja-build, valgrind, and Python 3.10 network chaos testbed in /app. Starter code includes RPC message abstractions, Raft state machine interfaces, storage backend contracts, and basic mock transport harnesses.
oracleStrategy: Reference C++20 implementation under solution/ provides a fully asynchronous, event-driven Raft engine implementing Pre-Vote, Joint Consensus, snapshot stream serialization, and linearizable ReadIndex queries.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes four verification channels:
1. Unit & Cluster Election Tests (3-node and 5-node basic leader election and log replication).
2. Jepsen-style Network Chaos Partitions (simulating dynamic partitions, bridge partitions, packet loss, and leader isolation).
3. Dynamic Membership Changes (adding/removing nodes under continuous client traffic without downtime).
4. Linearizable Read & Sanitizer Checks (validating linearizability of client read histories and 0 ASan defects).
binarySuccessCondition: Passes 100% of network chaos partition tests, completes dynamic membership reconfigurations without split-brain, guarantees linearizability, and passes 0 sanitizer errors.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 25%: Basic leader election & log replication under normal operation.
- 25%: Snapshot transfer (InstallSnapshot) & log compaction.
- 25%: Pre-Vote resilience under asymmetric partitions.
- 25%: Joint consensus membership transitions & linearizable reads.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Single-node centralized master bypass: Verifier simulates isolated virtual cluster nodes and verifies inter-node RPC exchanges.
2. In-memory unpersisted log hacks: Verifier crashes processes and checks disk storage state against recovered logs.
